results.fact: Time from trailhead to the plateau
results.correct_value: The plateau is reached at the top of the switchbacks, about 0.4-0.5 mi and ~400 ft from the lot, roughly 20-30 min; the first switchback is only a few hundred feet from the car.
results.evidence: The approach, beta, climbing_route, approach_variants and itinerary schedule (+20 min top of switchbacks) all place the plateau at ~400 ft of gain and under half a mile; only partner_requirements says 45 min-1 hr (and 15-30 min just to the base of switchbacks that start a few hundred feet from the car). WTA states the first ~400 ft of gain tops out on the table and the whole outing is 2.6 mi RT/725 ft; the Forest Service page puts the steep southeast-face climb within ~1 mile; a hiking guide gives 1.5-2 hr for the whole round trip at moderate pace, incompatible with up to an hour just to the plateau. No source states a minute figure, so this rests on the row plus the external distance/gain agreement.

results.correct_value: Class 3-4 (exposed 3rd-class scrambling with short 4th-class steps; Peak 1 often roped)
results.evidence: grade, overview, the notch waypoint, the summit waypoint, itinerary notes, partner_requirements and seasonal_hazards.exposure all say 3rd/4th class; only alpine_grade, beta, rope_note and one seasonal_guidance month say Class 3. A detailed first-hand trip report of all four peaks records 4th-class sections in the approach gully, at the notch to Peak 2, into the Peaks 3/4 notch, and a 4th/low-5th crux on Peak 1 where the party used a rope and rappelled; the SummitPost peak page (apparently the same author) says all four require exposed 3rd and 4th class scrambling. An older statement that all four are 'reportedly 3rd class' is the source of the outlier copies.

results.fact: Distance and gain from Twin Lakes to High Pass
results.evidence: The only outlier is bivy[1] (High Pass camp) notes, part of the regional camp list owned by the camping clean-up; approach, pitch_detail and waypoints agree on ~1.8-2 mi. High Pass camp and Twin Lakes basin camp do serve this route; the Twin Lakes Road pullouts entry is a road note rather than a camp. No bivy patch written.

results.correct_value: No glacier travel (trail, scree, seasonal snow and loose rock)
results.evidence: The row's own corrections note and seasonal_hazards.crevasses say no glacier is crossed, and the first-hand trip report describes only snow patches, scree and a basin traverse to the gully, no glacier. The conflict is in the route NAME ('Glacier/Scramble Route'), which this pass may not change; settling it needs a rename by the owner.

gain_ft (and loss_ft) say 3,400 ft while the itinerary day and totalNote say 3,200 ft. No outside source found states a car-to-car gain for this route, so neither is changed; a published round-trip gain figure would settle it.

dist_km 12.1 (7.5 mi, shown as 'Approach (one way)') equals the itinerary's 7.5 mi ROUND trip, while the waypoints put the summit ~4 mi from the trailhead. No outside source found states the one-way distance for this route, so dist_km is left alone; a sourced one-way mileage would settle it.
